newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Pasminco says better 2nd half possible.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Pasminco says better 2nd half possible.

text.p: Base metals miner Pasminco Ltd said on Wednesday it expected a stronger performance in the six months to June 30 if the recent rise in the zinc price and a weaker Australian dollar were maintained.

"If that were maintained, yes, that would give us a stronger six months but the market has been quite volatile so I am very cautious what they might end up at," chief executive David Stewart told reporters.

Pasminco earlier announced a flat net profit of A$20.2 million for the six months to December 31 and said it would pay a dividend based on its financial results for the 1996/97 year (July-June) if current market conditions are maintained.
It said the price of Pasminco's major commodity, zinc, has risen since the half-year end and is currently trading above the level it averaged during the December 1996 half-year.
Pasminco said the combined impact of external factors -- metal prices and exchange rates -- reduced earnings by about A$5 million for the half year.
The most significant adverse factor was the strength of the Australian dollar, it said.
The average U.S. dollar/Australian dollar exchange rate was 79.30 U.S. cents in the latest half-year, 4.8 cents higher than the 74.5 cents average rate for the corresponding period in 1995.
The Australian dollar was trading around US$0.7740 on Wednesday.
